newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FIGURE SKATING-MODEST LIPINSKI ON COURSE FOR TITLE.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-MODEST LIPINSKI ON COURSE FOR TITLE.

text.p: Tara Lipinski stayed on course to become the youngest ever figure skating world champion after winning the short programme on Friday but insisted she was not allowing herself to think about overall victory.

Maintaining the imperious form which brought her the U.S. National and Champions Series titles over the past month, the 14-year-old Texan, dancing to music from the film "Little Women", leads Vanessa Gusmeroli of France going into Saturday's decisive free skating.
"I think if I thought I could win this it would put too much pressure on me," said Lipinski.
"I'd just like another clean programme and it would be great to place or even finish fourth or fifth.
"I was pleased to do a clean short because I messed it up last year and this has given me a lot of confidence," added the American who last year was 23rd after the short before advancing to 15th.
Waiting a full minute of her two minutes 40 seconds routine before launching her first jump, Lipinski achieved a fine triple lutz-double toe loop combination.

She seemed to be wrongly positioned in the air on her triple flip but still landed it cleanly and her triple axel was fine. All were completed with her extra-fast spins in the air because she does not get very high off the ice when she takes off.
She received four scores of 5.8 for technique and four more 5.8s for presentation as she collected first place votes from five of the nine judges.
While the 1.47 metres, 35 kg Lipinski continued to defy her relative lack of experience, her big-name team mates struggled.

Defending champion Michelle Kwan, who saw Lipinski take her two other titles in recent weeks, messed up her combination jump and finished fourth. She two-footed the landing of the triple-lutz part of the combination.
"I waited a little too long and couldn't get out of it quickly enough," Kwan said. "My body was gone but my legs were still there."
Nicole Bobek, skating a day after the death of her coach, Carlo Fassi, was accompanied by Fassi's widow Christa before and after her programme.
She over-rotated her opening triple lutz and put both hands and one knee down landing a triple toe loop as she placed eighth.
"My warm-up felt great but right before the programme I looked at Christa and began crying," Bobek said.
"I was able to refocus my energy on what I needed to do, but my landings were not strong."

China's 1995 champion Chen Lu, completely out of form after missing four months of training with a foot injury, failed in her objective of qualifying for next winter's Olympics in Japan by placing 25th and not reaching Saturday's free final.
That was one place below what was needed to ensure Olympic qualification. She will now face a skate-off later in the year which will fill the last six places for the 30-woman field in Nagano.
Gusmeroli took three first-place votes to edge Russian Maria Butryskaya into third. Hungarian Krisztina Czako and European champion Irina Slutskaya of Russia were fifth and sixth respectively.
Gusmeroli, sixth in January's European championships after being third in the short programme, has improved in a short time.
"The competition really starts tomorrow," she said. "I learned a good lesson at the Europeans where my long programme did not go as well. I feel I can go forward now."
Gusmeroli, who also competes in water skiing, produced an unusual combination of triple lutz-double loop and skated strongly throughout.
Butyrskaya picked up the other first place vote with an Egyptian dance.
